identity.title: Detailed lens modeling and kinematics of the submillimeter galaxy G09v1.97: An analysis of CO, H<SUB>2</SUB>O, H<SUB>2</SUB>O<SUP>+</SUP>, and dust continuum emission

paper_type_evidence.quote: The current paper utilizes very high angular-resolution ALMA observations ($\approx 0''.1$) of G09v1.97, achieving scales of a few hundred parsecs in the source plane, to study the ISM using the emission from the dust, CO(6–5), ($2_{11} - 2_{02}$), hereafter H$_2$O and $^+$ ($2_{02}\text{--}1_{11}$), hereafter H$_2$O$^{+}$.
G09v1.97 was observed in band 4 with ALMA as part of project ID 2018.1.01710.S (P.I. Yang).

To be able to study the fainter $^+$ emission line, we combined the data presented above with lower-spatial-resolution observations (C36-5 configuration with baseline range 0.02–1.5 km) used in (cite: Yang19) (project ID: 2015.1.01320.S, P.I.: Omont).

evidence.quote: We aim to use high angular resolution observations of dust continuum, CO(6–5), H$_2$O($2_{11} - 2_{02}$), and H$_2$O$^{+}$($2_{02}\text{--}1_{11}$) emission to constrain the ongoing processes in the $z = 3.63$ gravitationally lensed submillimeter galaxy H-ATLAS J083051.0+013224 (G09v1.97).

evidence.loc: Physical properties of the warm rotating disk G09v1.97

method.value: Extract continuum flux and molecular line spectra from the expected emission region of Yang19; fit asymmetric line profiles with double Gaussian profiles; compute moment-0 and moment-1 maps (clipping <3 sigma in moment-1); calculate line luminosities using Solomon97 formula.

evidence.quote: We extracted the continuum from the region of expected emission from (cite: Yang19), shown in Fig. [1](#fig:continuum).
We created moment-0 and moment-1 maps from the same region used to extract the spectra. For clarity, we removed flux at lower than $3\sigma$ levels in the moment-1 maps.
The spectrum was fit with a double Gaussian profile to account for the asymmetric line shape.

analysis_steps.goal: Perform parametric gravitational lens modeling on visibilities

method.value: Fit two foreground lens galaxies as single isothermal ellipsoid (SIE) mass profiles and the background source as a single linear Sérsic profile directly on the interferometric visibilities in PyAutoLens; optimize the lens mass model on dust continuum first, then fix the lens mass model to fit CO(6-5), H2O, and H2O+ emission.

evidence.quote: PyAutoLens is capable of handling interferometric data and performing reconstructions directly on the visibilities, thereby minimizing the effect of correlated noise in interferometric images.
We modeled these two galaxies as single isothermal ellipsoid (SIE) mass distributions.
We first model the dust continuum emission to obtain an optimized lens model and proceed to use this to reconstruct the molecular line emission.

key_parameters.value: Lens redshifts fixed at z = 0.626 (or 0.636 in text) and z = 1.002; 1000 posterior samples for magnification error

evidence.quote: We performed the sampling 1000 times for each emission type, obtained magnification factors for each of these samples, and calculated the standard deviation of the magnification factors from each sample, thus obtaining the magnification factor error.

assumptions.value: Two SIE lens mass profiles and a single Sérsic source profile

evidence.quote: We modeled these two galaxies as single isothermal ellipsoid (SIE) mass distributions.
We modeled the source as a single Sérsic profile using a linear light profile, allowing the intensity parameters to be solved via linear algebra.

fitting.value: Uniform priors on lens and source parameters; linear algebra solve for intensity; 1000 posterior samples from maximum likelihood solution for errors

evidence.quote: During lens modeling, the redshifts of the lens galaxies were fixed while we allowed all other parameters to vary, assuming uniform priors.
We modeled the source as a single Sérsic profile using a linear light profile, allowing the intensity parameters to be solved via linear algebra.

validation.value: Tested adding a second Sérsic source profile for CO(6-5) as in Yang19 and verified it did not improve residuals

evidence.quote: We attempted to improve the model by including a second source, also described by a Sérsic profile and as motivated by (cite: Yang19). However, the inclusion of this second source did not improve the residuals, and we discarded this model.

analysis_steps.goal: Perform non-parametric pixelated source-plane reconstructions and reconstruct the de-magnified CO(6-5) spectral cube

method.value: Using the continuum-optimized lens mass model, reconstruct source-plane emission on a magnification-weighted adaptive Voronoi pixel mesh with constant regularization in PyAutoLens; bin CO(6-5) into 50 km/s channels, reconstruct each bin non-parametrically, and interpolate onto a square pixel grid to form a de-magnified spectral cube; compute source-plane error maps from lens posterior sampling and visibility covariance matrix (via CASA STATWT).

evidence.quote: In this work, we use the optimized lens mass model derived from the dust continuum emission (described in Section [3.3.1.1](#subsubsec:parametric_dust_lens_model)) to create a pixelized reconstruction using a magnification weighted adaptive Voronoi pixel mesh.

To create de-magnified source-plane emission cubes, we divided the emission line into bins of equivalent size and non-parametrically modeled the emission in each bin. We used a spectral resolution of $\approx 50$ km/s

In our case, this matrix is computed directly from the interferometric visibilities in the uv-plane and corresponding visibility errors extracted using CASA’s STATWT task, as described in Equation 8 of (cite: Enia18).

key_parameters.value: Circular region of radius 1.5 arcsec (11 kpc); CO(6-5) cube spectral resolution ~50 km/s; static source-plane beam of 0.035'' x 0.027'' (5 pixels per beam); 1000 samples for sigma_l; 100 samples for pixelized magnification error

evidence.quote: We used this methodology to create pixelized reconstructions of the dust continuum emission, CO(6–5), , and $^+$ emission using a Voronoi mesh covering a circular region of radius 1.5 arcseconds (11 kpc) in the image plane around G09v1.97.
Thus, the static angular resolution achieved in the source plane was approximately $0''.035 \times 0''.027$ ($\approx 260 \times 200$ pc) for the reconstructed CO(6–5) spectral cube.

The pixelization magnification factor error comes from sampling the maximum-likelihood lens model 100 times, and creating pixelized image and source plane emission maps for each sample where the magnification error is the standard deviation of the magnification factor across these 100 samples.

assumptions.value: Static source-plane beam defined as theta_maj/sqrt(mu) x theta_min/sqrt(mu) with 5 pixels per beam; Gaussian distribution of lens model parameters over 1000 samples

evidence.quote: We assumed a standard beam size of five pixels per source-plane beam, where the source-plane beam was defined as $\theta_{\rm maj}/\sqrt{\mu} \times \theta_{\rm min}/\sqrt{\mu}$, with $\mu$ given by the parametrically modeled CO(6–5) emission (see Table [\[tab:lensing_bestfit_sourceparams\]](#tab:lensing_bestfit_sourceparams)).
This approach is valid only if the lens model parameters form Gaussian distributions over the 1000 samples. We confirmed that this assumption holds.

fitting.value: Magnification-weighted adaptive Voronoi pixel mesh with constant regularization scheme

evidence.quote: We used a constant regularization scheme parameterized by the regularization coefficient.

validation.value: Compared moment-0 and moment-1 maps on Voronoi pixels versus interpolated square pixels; also tested doubling the number of Voronoi pixels and using a rectangular mesh

evidence.quote: We computed moment-0 and moment-1 maps for the Voronoi pixels and visually verified that the interpolation to square pixels did not significantly affect the moment-0 or moment-1 maps.
In the first, we used twice the number of pixels in the Voronoi mesh prior to interpolation to a square grid, and in the second, we used a rectangular mesh instead of a Voronoi mesh.

analysis_steps.goal: Model source-plane CO(6-5) kinematics and classify disk vs. merger

method.value: Fit tilted rings to the de-magnified source-plane CO(6-5) spectral cube using 3DBarolo (first with PA and inclination free, then fixing them to their averages and refitting); calculate PVsplit parameters from the major-axis PV diagram to test disk vs. merger classification.

evidence.quote: We use $^{\rm 3D}$Barolo to model the kinematics of the CO(6–5) emission in the source plane.

We first ran the fitting procedure with both position angle and inclination free (together with the rotation velocity and dispersion). We then took the averages of the position angle and the inclination, respectively, and fixed those values to refit the disk.
Nonetheless, we calculate the PVsplit parameters for G09v1.97 and find: $P_{\rm major} = -1.56$, $P_{\mathrm V} = -0.33$, and $P_{\mathrm R} = 0.50$.

key_parameters.value: Smooth & Search masking with 3 sigma cut; 11 rings with radial separation 0.0138'' (theta_maj / 2.5); center fixed via 2D-Gaussian fit to moment-0 map; fixed i = 50 deg and PA = 6.7 deg

evidence.quote: We use $^{\rm 3D}$Barolo ’s Smooth & Search algorithm to mask the data. This algorithm first smooths the data, performs a $3\sigma$ cut to the data to mask values at $<3\sigma$, and then searches for sources in the smoothed and masked data.

We use a radial separation of $0.0138''$ for the individual rings, calculated by $\theta_{\rm maj}/2.5$ where $\theta_{\rm maj}$ is the major axis of the source-plane static beam, resulting in 11 rings.
The inclination ($i$), at 50 degrees, did not vary at all, and the position angle varied from $\approx 1$ to $\approx 19$ degrees, resulting in an average of $(6.7 \pm 1.7)^{\circ}$.

assumptions.value: Static source-plane beam of 0.035'' x 0.027''; V_rot in the outermost ring approximates V_max

evidence.quote: We perform all kinematic modeling on the CO(6–5) source plane de-magnified cube (see Section [3.3.3](#subsec:cube_and_spec_reconstructions)), assuming a static beam in the source plane.
therefore we assume that using $\rm V_{rot}$ in the outermost ring is the best approximation of $\rm V_{max}$ possible with the current data.

fitting.value: Monte Carlo evaluation of tilted-ring model parameters in 3DBarolo

evidence.quote: Rather than employing a parametric approach, this tool fits a user-specific number of tilted rings to the input emission line cube and returns the best-fit model for the rings through a Monte Carlo evaluation methodology.

validation.value: Varied ring separation from 0.007'' (23 rings) to 0.042'' (4 rings) in steps of a factor of 2 to test impact of static beam assumption

evidence.quote: We performed a simple investigation into the impact of the assumed static beam on our kinematic modeling results by varying the ring separation used in the $^{\rm 3D}$Barolo modeling. We vary the separation from $0''.007$ ($\theta_{\rm maj}/5$, corresponding to 23 rings) to $0''.042$ ($\theta_{\rm maj}*1.2$, corresponding to 4 rings) in steps of a factor of two.

claims.hypothesis: G09v1.97 is composed of two separate merging/interacting galaxies in the source plane, as concluded by earlier lower-resolution parametric lens modeling (Yang et al. 2019).
claims.experiment: Perform both parametric (Sérsic) and non-parametric (adaptive Voronoi mesh) visibility-plane lens modeling in PyAutoLens using ~0.1'' ALMA observations of dust continuum, CO(6-5), H2O, and H2O+, including a de-magnified 50 km/s CO(6-5) spectral cube.
claims.result: A single source profile fits all emission types with small residuals (<= 2-3 sigma); adding a second Sérsic source does not improve residuals, and non-parametric reconstructions of red and blue velocity bins show co-spatial emission connected by a smooth south-north velocity gradient.
claims.finding: G09v1.97 does not require two separate sources; it is a single source whose apparent red and blue components arise from differential magnification across a rotating velocity gradient.

evidence.quote: We find that our lens modeling results do not require more than one source, contrary to what has been found in previous studies.

We attempted to improve the model by including a second source, also described by a Sérsic profile and as motivated by (cite: Yang19). However, the inclusion of this second source did not improve the residuals, and we discarded this model.
We suggest that the discrepancy between the results provided in (cite: Yang19) and those found in this work stems primarily from the velocity gradient found in the source plane.

claims.hypothesis: The source-plane spatial extents of dust continuum, CO(6-5), and H2O(2_11-2_02) trace the same star-forming region in G09v1.97.
claims.experiment: Compare normalized percentage contour maps and enclosed flux in circular apertures from non-parametric source-plane reconstructions of dust continuum, CO(6-5), and H2O.
claims.result: CO(6-5) and H2O spatial distributions match closely (with CO(6-5) slightly more extended), while the dust continuum emission is more compact.
claims.finding: CO(6-5) and H2O trace similar extended star-forming gas, whereas the dust continuum appears more compact likely due to dust temperature and optical depth gradients.

evidence.quote: We find that the regions of CO(6–5) and H$_2$O($2_{11} - 2_{02}$) emission match closely in the source plane but that the dust continuum emission is more compact.
Overall, the distribution of the CO(6–5) emission closely matches that of the while the continuum appears more compact.

claims.hypothesis: G09v1.97 is a rotationally supported disk galaxy with potential non-circular perturbations from recent or ongoing interactions.
claims.experiment: Model the de-magnified source-plane CO(6-5) spectral cube with 3DBarolo tilted rings, evaluate V_max/sigma_bar and PVsplit metrics, and analyze velocity residuals and gas depletion time.
claims.result: 3DBarolo yields V_max = 388 (+55/-36) km/s, average sigma = 138 (+7/-6) km/s, and V_max/sigma_bar = 2.8 ± 0.4, along with ~6 sigma non-circular velocity residuals (>125 km/s) and a short depletion time of 13 ± 8 Myr.
claims.finding: G09v1.97 is dominated by ordered rotation as a warm rotating disk, but exhibits statistically significant non-circular motions (tidal tail, outflow, or companion) and rapid gas consumption triggered by a recent interaction or merger.

evidence.quote: We perform kinematic modeling on the source-plane CO(6–5) emission line cube using $^{\rm 3D}$Barolo and find that the kinematics are well explained as a rotating disk with a maximum rotational velocity of $\rm V_{max} = 388^{+55}_{-36}$ km/s and an average dispersion of $\bar{\sigma} = 138^{+7}_{-6}$ km/s, implying $\rm V_{max} / \sigma = 2.8 \pm 0.4$.
These residuals cannot be explained by the lensing analysis and source plane cube reconstruction, and are statistically significant ($\sim 6\sigma$).

In this scenario, G09v1.97 has recently settled into a turbulent, rotating disk that is rapidly consuming its gas and showing non-disk morphological features due to likely recent or on-going interactions or merger events.

why_this_data.value: High angular resolution (~0.1'') ALMA observations combined with gravitational lensing magnification (mu ~ 6-10) probe physical scales of a few hundred parsecs in the source plane to resolve the ISM and kinematics; lower-resolution archival data are combined to detect the faint H2O+ line.

evidence.quote: The current paper utilizes very high angular-resolution ALMA observations ($\approx 0''.1$) of G09v1.97, achieving scales of a few hundred parsecs in the source plane, to study the ISM using the emission from the dust, CO(6–5), ($2_{11} - 2_{02}$), hereafter H$_2$O and $^+$ ($2_{02}\text{--}1_{11}$), hereafter H$_2$O$^{+}$.

To be able to study the fainter $^+$ emission line, we combined the data presented above with lower-spatial-resolution observations (C36-5 configuration with baseline range 0.02–1.5 km) used in (cite: Yang19) (project ID: 2015.1.01320.S, P.I.: Omont).

why_this_method.value: PyAutoLens fits directly in the visibility plane to minimize correlated noise and uses a magnification-weighted adaptive Voronoi mesh to avoid a priori morphological assumptions (disk vs. merger); 3DBarolo fits tilted rings with PA and inclination fixed to their averages so residuals reveal non-axisymmetric structures.

evidence.quote: PyAutoLens is capable of handling interferometric data and performing reconstructions directly on the visibilities, thereby minimizing the effect of correlated noise in interferometric images. Additionally, PyAutoLens can create source plane pixelizations from interferometric data, which eliminates the need for assumptions about the background galaxy’s morphology.

By fixing the position angle and inclination, we ensure that the final fit most closely resembles a disk, and the residuals retain the ability to reveal the presence of non-axisymmetric structures such as outflows, tidal tails, etc.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Two-source parametric Sérsic lens model for CO(6-5): tested as motivated by Yang19, but discarded because it did not improve the residuals.

evidence.quote: We attempted to improve the model by including a second source, also described by a Sérsic profile and as motivated by (cite: Yang19). However, the inclusion of this second source did not improve the residuals, and we discarded this model.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Voronoi mesh interpolation artifacts as the cause of kinematic residuals: tested by doubling the number of Voronoi pixels and by using a rectangular mesh instead of a Voronoi mesh, and rejected because very similar residuals remained.

evidence.quote: In the first, we used twice the number of pixels in the Voronoi mesh prior to interpolation to a square grid, and in the second, we used a rectangular mesh instead of a Voronoi mesh. In both cases, we found very similar residuals, suggesting that the interpolation from the Voronoi mesh to the square pixel grid was not the cause of the residuals.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Obscured AGN contamination of L_IR and SFR: considered and rejected because no compact central excess is seen in CO(6-5), H2O, or continuum maps, consistent with line-to-IR ratios and q-parameter.

limitations_admitted.value: CO(6-5) traces warmer, denser gas than CO(1-0) or [C II] and may not trace the full spatial extent of the colder molecular gas disk, and converting CO(6-5) to CO(1-0) and M_gas (with uncertain alpha_CO) is inherently uncertain.

evidence.quote: We note that CO(6–5) might not trace large distances into the disk of the galaxy, given the relatively high temperatures and densities necessary to excite mid-$J$ transitions of the CO molecule, in comparison to those necessary for CO(1–0), HII, or \[C ii\] , and is likely to not trace the spatial extent of the bulk colder molecular gas in G09v1.97 (cite: Cailli13; Madden20).
